resource.name: ASA Now · Foster-Youth Clothing, Hygiene and Baby Supplies
resource.description: Request essentials for a new foster placement or a young adult who has aged out of care.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Request socks, underwear, hygiene products, diapers, a backpack and a food box through the Immediate Needs form. Available items depend on the request and supplies.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For new placements from birth through age 18 with child-welfare involvement, and youth who have aged out of care through age 21. Provide a Notice to Provider, tribal child-welfare documentation or proof of previous involvement for an aged-out youth. The form’s income question does not determine eligibility.

**How to Best Connect**
Open Assistance on the website and choose Immediate Needs. Complete one request per child and upload the required proof. Staff say they will text within 24 hours to confirm pickup. Call or text 480-415-4481 if you need help.

**Access**
Pickup is in Mesa on Tuesday or Thursday, 9 a.m.–6 p.m. Call or text after submitting if you need another day, an evening or a weekend appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Beds and car seats generally require a referral to another agency. Kinship caregivers needing a car seat should call after submitting. The separate food-request form currently directs people to call or text; the Immediate Needs form also includes a food-box request.
resource.hours: Confirmed pickup: Tuesday and Thursday, 9 a.m.–6 p.m.; other times by arrangement.

resource.name: Clothes Cabin · Clothing, Workwear, Linens and Hygiene
resource.description: Free clothes, shoes and linens in Gilbert. No appointment or referral; bring photo ID or ask about a temporary ID accommodation.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
One Small Step’s Clothes Cabin gives free clothing, shoes, household linens and hygiene items. Back to Work helps with required workwear and a pair of work shoes for a new job. Unsheltered clients can also use showers, weekly laundry, lockers and mailboxes.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For anyone who cannot afford the items needed. Clothing visits are once every three months, for yourself, your partner and your children under 18. Bring current photo ID of any kind; ask about a temporary accommodation if you are obtaining ID. Work items require new-hire papers, an employer letter or the Back to Work request form. Staff may ask for guardianship information when you collect clothing for children.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit during client hours; no appointment or referral is needed. For a new job, bring its clothing requirements and employment evidence. For help, call 480-285-4111 or email info@onesmallstepaz.org.

**Access**
The building is at the back of the business park. Children cannot enter the shopping area; if they come, they must stay in the small playroom or lobby. Arrive at least one hour before closing for showers and two hours before closing for laundry.

**Important Information to Know**
Quantities depend on stock. The FAQ usually allows 4–7 clothing items plus socks and underwear, and one set of sheets, one blanket or one set of towels per visit; ask about that day’s limits. Clothes Cabin closes for holidays, the day before Thanksgiving, the Christmas–New Year week and the last week of January. Donation and paid resale-shop hours differ from free client hours.
resource.address: 710 N. Cooper Road, Gilbert, AZ 85233; back of Cottonwood Professional Plaza

resource.name: House of Refuge · Resident Clothing, Furniture and Household Goods
resource.description: Free household items for families enrolled in House of Refuge housing. Public food-bank access is a separate service.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
House of Refuge families can shop for clothing, furniture and household essentials at no cost. Items remain theirs when they leave the housing program. A toy closet offers birthday gifts for residents’ children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
This non-food shopping is for House of Refuge program families. General-public access to clothing and furniture is not established. Housing has a separate application, eligibility screening, rent and move-in costs; free goods do not mean housing is free.

**How to Best Connect**
Residents should arrange shopping with their caseworker or call Helping Hands at 480-988-9395. Email donationcenter@houseofrefuge.org. For housing intake, call 480-988-9242 or use the provider’s Need Housing page.

**Access**
The center is at 6858 E. Ursula Avenue, separate from the administrative office. Its August–September notice lists Monday and Friday, 10 AM–4 PM, and weekend closure, but leaves the other weekdays unclear. Confirm resident-shopping times with staff.

**Important Information to Know**
Do not send someone to collect furniture simply because the center accepts donations. The separate public food bank accepts people without an appointment or ID; its availability does not establish public access to clothing, toys or furniture.
resource.address: Helping Hands House: 6858 E. Ursula Avenue, Mesa, AZ 85212
resource.hours: Residents: arrange shopping with staff; confirm current center hours

resource.name: Valley Bloom · School Clothing, Shoes and Essentials
resource.description: School-arranged clothing, shoes and basic supplies for students in need. Start with the child’s school nurse or counselor.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Formerly Assistance League of East Valley. Valley Bloom provides school clothing, uniforms, shoes and hygiene kits. Students experiencing homelessness in grades 6–12 may also receive bedding, transit passes and snacks. Graduating seniors can ask about its scholarships.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Schools identify students with the greatest need. Clothing events focus on kindergarten–grade 6; homeless-teen support covers grades 6–12. Partners include Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Kyrene and Tempe Elementary school districts.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the school nurse, counselor or family-support worker about Valley Bloom clothing help. School staff arrange the referral. For program questions, call 480-792-1600 or email info@valleybloom.org.

**Access**
Help is coordinated with schools; it is not a confirmed walk-in giveaway at the Chandler thrift shop. Ask the school about the next clothing event or help available between events.

**Important Information to Know**
Tell school staff about urgent shoes, uniforms or hygiene needs. What is provided depends on the program and school arrangements. Scholarship help has separate selection rules; it is not automatic for every student.
resource.address: Through participating schools; office/thrift shop: 2326 N. Alma School Road, Chandler
resource.hours: School-arranged services; thrift shop hours are separate

resource.name: CarePortal · Furniture, Clothing and Household Essentials by Referral
resource.description: A participating caseworker can request needed household items to help keep children safe and families together.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
Participating agencies ask local churches and community partners for items such as beds, furniture, clothing, diapers and household necessities. Help depends on someone being able to meet the request.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For children and families facing a crisis, including child-welfare, foster, adoption and aging-out situations. Religious membership is not required.

**How to Best Connect**
Ask your DCS worker, school support worker or other child-serving caseworker whether their agency uses CarePortal. Explain the item needed and how it will help the child. A participating worker must approve and submit the request; families cannot submit their own.

**Access**
Discuss pickup or delivery with the worker when a partner offers help. CarePortal operates locally, including through a Mesa church partner; agency participation varies.

**Important Information to Know**
Give the worker permission before your need is shared. Public requests should describe the need without your name, address or other identifying details. If no partner responds, ask the worker about another route.
resource.address: Start with your participating child-serving agency or caseworker.

resource.name: Phoenix Electrical JATC · Paid Electrician Apprenticeship
resource.description: Train as an electrician while working for a contractor. Admission is competitive, and both application and training fees apply.
resource.informationText:
**Programs and Services**
A four-year program combines paid work with classroom training. Selected apprentices are assigned to a participating contractor.

**Eligibility Requirements**
You must be 18 by the start and meet education and algebra requirements or approved alternatives. Identification and school records are needed. Some military service or documented electrical experience can qualify for exceptions. You must be able to reach regional work sites. Work can involve ladders, confined spaces and regular lifting of 50 pounds; ask the program about its essential job requirements and accommodations.

**How to Best Connect**
Use How to Apply on the program website. Email webservices@pejatc.org for application help or to arrange use of a training-center computer.

**Access**
Training centers are in Phoenix; work sites vary across the program area. Classes accompany full-time work. Check the current application deadline before paying.

**Important Information to Know**
Published charges are a $40 nonrefundable application fee and $187 monthly during training. Confirm current costs. Applying does not guarantee selection.
resource.address: Phoenix training centers; regional job sites
